derivations.claim: Each term $c_nI(x-s_n)$ lies in $[0,c_n]$, so the partial sums are nondecreasing and bounded above by $\sum_n c_n$; [L1] gives convergence and defines $\alpha(x)$ with $0\le\alpha(x)\le\sum_n c_n$.

Monotonicity of $I$ gives $I(x-s_n)\le I(y-s_n)$ for $x\le y$; multiplying by $c_n\ge0$ and passing to the limit by [L1] makes $\alpha$ nondecreasing, and $\alpha=\alpha-0$ with [L2] gives bounded variation.

[L6] supplies $M\ge0$ with $|f|\le M$ on the compact $[a,b]$; $0\le|c_nf(s_n)|\le Mc_n$ and [L8] give absolute convergence of $\sum c_nf(s_n)$; step 2.1 and [L3] give existence of $\int_a^b f\,d\alpha$.

For a single interior jump $\sigma=I(\cdot-s)$, exactly one partition index has $t_i\le s<t_{i+1}$ and increment $1$, so the Stieltjes sum of [L7] equals $f(\xi_i)$ with $|\xi_i-s|<\delta$; continuity [L9] gives $\int_a^b f\,d\sigma=f(s)$, and [L2] gives $\sigma$ bounded variation.
Finitely many applications of the integrator-linearity [L4], each summand evaluated by step 1.2, give $\int_a^b f\,d\alpha_N=\sum_{n<N}c_nf(s_n)$.

The tail $\beta_N=\alpha-\alpha_N$ is nondecreasing with bounded variation by the argument of steps 1.1 and 2.1; $s_n\in(a,b)$ gives $\beta_N(a)=0$ and $\beta_N(b)=\sum_{n\ge N}c_n$, and every partition sum of a nondecreasing function telescopes, so [L2] gives $\operatorname{Var}_{[a,b]}(\beta_N)=\sum_{n\ge N}c_n$.
[L3] makes both $\int f\,d\alpha_N$ and $\int f\,d\beta_N$ exist, [L4] splits $\int f\,d\alpha$ along $\alpha=\alpha_N+\beta_N$, and step 2.2 with [L5] bounds the difference by $M\sum_{n\ge N}c_n$.
Convergence of $\sum c_n$ drives its tails to $0$, so the partial sums $\sum_{n<N}c_nf(s_n)$ converge to $\int_a^b f\,d\alpha$; step 3.1 gives absolute convergence and [L1], [L9] identify the sum.
